intro: In İstanbul province, above the Eminönü market, rises Rüstem Pasha Mosque, a mosque and complex built in 1561–1563. This is Sinan's mosque, sheathed inside and out in İznik tiles at a density no other Ottoman building attempts.
history: Sinan built this mosque for Rüstem Pasha, Süleyman's grand vizier and son-in-law. It sits above the Eminönü market on a platform formed by the shops beneath it, an arrangement that both funded the mosque and lifted it above the crowd. Step inside and you will see why it is celebrated: its İznik tiling, inside and out, is denser than in any other Ottoman mosque.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the İznik tile panels and the platform over the market. Pause at the entrance porch, and notice the stair approaches.
facts: Did you know? The tomato red in these tiles is a colour the İznik workshops could produce only for a short period, and this mosque is its largest single application, so look closely for it. The mosque also sits on a platform formed by the shops of the Eminönü market beneath it: they funded it and lifted it above the crowd at once.
outro: This brings our tour of Rüstem Pasha Mosque to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These tiles have kept their colours for centuries; let them keep shining for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
